name: BlogCutter Activity Log & Security Audit
author: Blog Cutter AI

sections.description:
BlogCutter Activity Log & Security Audit provides site administrators with a clear record of activities occurring on their WordPress installation. It helps you monitor specific actions, identify who performed them, and review when they occurred.

This plugin is designed for performance and clarity, featuring a modern dashboard, paginated log views, and user-controlled storage management.

🛡️ Key Features

  • Real-Time Activity Tracking: Monitor user logins, content modifications, and system updates.
  • User Monitoring: Track successful logins, failed login attempts (security auditing), and logouts.
  • Content Audit: Record when users create, update, or delete posts and pages.
  • System Surveillance: Logs when plugins are activated/deactivated or when site settings are modified.
  • Traffic Hits: Optional tracking for public visitor URL hits to monitor site traffic.
  • Modern Dashboard: A clean, card-based interface for analyzing site events.
  • User-Defined Rotation: Control your server storage by setting a custom log size limit (e.g., 2MB, 5MB, or 20MB).
  • Performance Optimized: Features 100-row pagination to ensure the dashboard remains fast regardless of log size.
  • Export Data: Download your activity history as a CSV file for external review.

🚀 Performance & Maintenance

  1. Lightweight Logging: Optimized to ensure minimal impact on site speed.
  2. Auto-Cleanup: The “Vault” automatically rotates based on your defined MB limit to prevent large file sizes.
  3. Data Privacy: All audit data is stored locally in a protected directory on your server.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the blogcutter-activity-log-security-audit folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Access BlogCutter Log from your WordPress admin sidebar.
  4. Set your preferred storage limits under BlogCutter Log > Settings.
sections.faq:
How does the auto-rotation work?

In the settings page, you can define a limit in Megabytes (MB). Once the log file exceeds this size, the plugin automatically wipes the old data to protect your server storage.

Does this plugin track every user role?

Yes, you can toggle tracking for administrators, authors, and public guests independently in the settings.

Where is the log data stored?

Data is stored in a secure .log file within your WordPress uploads directory, protected by a .htaccess file to prevent public access.
